This modest initial mass is characteristic of altricial picids, which require extensive parental care. Field records indicate that the ultimate wet weight achieved by adult females of this species reaches approximately 114 grams [Wwi = approximately 114 grams], a value that reflects a substantial increase of roughly eighteen-fold from the birth weight. This considerable growth trajectory is supported by the sustained provisioning efforts of both parents over the nestling period, during which the brood is fed a diet rich in arboreal ants and beetle larvae.
